verdict.rationale: DBOS documents an OpenAPI-described HTTP API and the dbosctl CLI for Conductor. Together they cover workflow, queue and schedule management, app registration and settings, metrics, audit logs, members, roles and API keys, so most of what the Conductor dashboard does is reachable programmatically. The library's DBOSClient also offers programmatic access to workflows. No doc states full UI/API parity, though: dashboard actions like pause and resume are not explicitly listed in the API scope, and the probe found no OpenAPI spec at the standard doc paths. missing for 10: an explicit UI-to-API parity statement, documented API coverage of pause/resume/restart-from-step, a publicly retrievable OpenAPI spec, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Conductor's workflow, queue, and schedule management is available over an OpenAPI-described HTTP API and from the dbosctl command-line client, so you can script incident response and wire Conductor into your own tooling.

register applications with Conductor and tune their settings, search workflows, cancel or fork them, inspect queues and schedules, drive schedules, read metrics and audit logs, and manage members, roles, and API keys.
dbosctl is a command-line client for the Conductor API. It manages workflows, queues, schedules, applications, and API keys against DBOS-managed Conductor or a self-hosted Conductor
DBOSClient provides a programmatic way to interact with your DBOS application from external code or from another DBOS application.
